study-design: 20M, with a separate 37M backbone variant. Scratch budgets extend to 160 TPP.
Matched 20M candidate and control. Each conversion pair shares an AR parent within a seed.
Next-token prediction with the same input canvas, and reconstruction under each model's trained attention pattern where available.
Six sizes, 20M--477M. Scratch 40 versus AR 20 + diffusion 20, using AdamW.
Full-sequence diffusion bound on 1,024 packed validation rows.

replication-coverage: LLaDA 1

Compared with scratch MDLM, sample mask rates independently across rows, raise the lower bound from 0 to 0.001, randomly crop the batch with 1\% probability, and include MASK in the training softmax. Both arms use inverse-time weighting.
At 20 TPP the next-token loss difference was $+0.009$ BPB. The document interval includes zero.
LLaDA 1.5
Compare preference-loss estimators on the same 32 fixed preference pairs.
Sharing noise between policy and reference reduced estimator variance. We did not train a preference-optimized model.
LLaDA 2.0
Grow block length from 1 to 1,024, hold there, then shrink to 32. Compare with fixed length 32. Both receive AR10, 28 TPP of conversion and a final 2 TPP at length 32.
The curriculum raised next-token loss in both seeds. Mean conversion time fell from 52.4 to 40.7 minutes.
LLaDA 2.1
Train a model to replace visible tokens as well as fill masks. Test repairs against the original text and test whether clean drafts survive.
Repair improved on familiar grounded formats. Transfer to ordinary text remained weak.
LLaDA 2.2
Reconstruct delete/merge-style edits and compare with positional repair using the same action vocabulary.
General structural repair remained weak. Unspecified training choices limit fidelity to the published system.
BD3-LM
Compare block-noise calibration with a fixed mask-probability range at 20 TPP.
Calibration lowered next-token loss with masks to the block end. Using one mask reversed the ranking in both seeds.
Fast-dLLM-v2
Compare two complementary, block-aligned masked views and shifted targets with fixed-block conversion from the same AR10 parent.
Lower next-token loss at equal source tokens. The smaller difference at matched estimated compute has an interval spanning zero.
Adaptive Block Diffusion \citep{jain2026adaptive}
Compare variable partitions with fixed blocks after MDLM initialization.
The ordering differed between next-token prediction and reconstruction.
WeDLM
Compare reordered attention with a bidirectional-current-block control.
Next-token loss favored reordering in a single-seed screen. Serving performance was outside this test.
